alignments.note: The ASV writes a word for the correlative μέν — *verily* — so it is aligned to it under rule 70 rather than left unrepresented.
ἀπών → *being absent*, the supplied participial copula riding with the participle.
The ASV gives σώματι no determiner, so under rule 21's determinerless clause the case preposition *in* stays with the noun.
No English determiner stands for the article to anchor, so it realizes nothing under rule 23.
παρών → *present*, the second participle sharing the first's supplied *being*.
*in spirit*, the case preposition staying with the determinerless noun under rule 21.
Article with no English determiner to anchor, unrepresented under rule 23.
κέκρικα → *have … judged*; the auxiliary rides with the verb under rule 9 and the head stands on the lexical *judged*, discontinuously under rule 15.
ὡς → *as though*, one clause-introducer; the archaic *though* is not split off, as rule 61 refuses to split *before that*. Head on *as*, the word glossing the adverb.
The participle is expanded into a finite clause *I were present*; the supplied subject and copula are rule 7 helpers on it, headed on the predicate word.
Substantival article before a participle supplies the pronoun *him* and nothing else under rule 32.
κατεργασάμενον → *that hath … wrought*, relativizer and auxiliary riding with the participle, headed on the lexical verb, discontinuously under rule 15.
οὕτως → *so*; no answering καί stands, so rule 100 is not in question.
Substantival demonstrative with a supplied generic noun; rule 17 heads on the demonstrative, as ταῦτα → *these things* does, no article standing here to claim the supplied noun.

review_notes: μέν is aligned to *verily* under rule 70's English-side test.
*as though* is kept whole on ὡς rather than split, on rule 61's refusal to split a two-word clause-introducer.
